children: Crude oil and refined product futures prices had backed off earlier highs but were still showing solid gains Tuesday as escalating fighting in the Persian Gulf region sent contracts higher.

U.S. oil prices were about 1.5% higher at 11:15 a.m. ET, with the October West Texas Intermediate crude contract ahead by $1.38 to $92.86/bbl after climbing as high as $94.73/bbl earlier. The November contract was trading $1.34 higher to $89.91/bbl.
Brent crude contracts were once again approaching the $100/bbl mark, with the November contract reaching as high as $99.46/bbl earlier before falling to $97.75/bbl, a gain of 75cts.

December Brent was ahead by 91cts to $94.07/bbl. ULSD futures were about 13cts/gal off earlier highs, with the October contract rising by 6.47cts to $4.6049/gal while November futures were trading up 7.09cts to $4.4646/gal.
RBOB futures had backed off earlier highs by about 2cts, with the front-month contract climbing 8.73cts to $3.3019/gal and November futures 8.01cts in the black to $3.0936/gal.

Prices are being supported Tuesday by reports that Houthis in Yemen launched attacks on energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. Those attacks, along with U.S. strikes on three Iranian tankers on Saturday, have renewed fears that a new flare-up in fighting could disrupt energy exports from the region.

The rising futures prices are likely to continue pressuring retail fuel prices in the U.S. even as the summer driving season has ended. U.S. retail gasoline prices on Tuesday rose for a third straight day to $4.1514/gal, up 0.09ct on the day but 5.6cts higher than a week earlier. U.S. retail diesel prices were averaging $5.9012/gal, 0.03ct lower than the new record set on Monday but still 26.87cts/gal higher than a week ago.

The prospect of higher energy prices was also helping send equity markets lower, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average down more than 500 pts, or 1%, heading into Tuesday afternoon. The NASDAQ Composite was about 20pts, or 0.07%, lower.
